title: MedicaSys air-gapped deployment workshop - action log and feasibility notes
summary: Notes and action items from Nov 7 workshop with MedicaSys (healthcare SaaS customer) — scoped air-gapped on-prem proof of concept. Goal: validate deployable package and minimal network egress model for a HIPAA-sensitive environment.
workshop_notes: Attendees: MedicaSys infra (N. Gomez, T. Huang), security (A. Rivera), apps (S. Lin), Redwood SEs (Marco, Priya), SRE (Liam). Session objectives: 1) confirm baseline infra inventory; 2) walk through proposed packaging options (airgapped container bundle vs. installable RPMs); 3) map network flows and offline key management options; 4) surface compliance questions and timeline for POC. High-level outcome: customer comfortable with our VPC-private control-plane approach but requires zero egress for model weights and optional control-plane replication to an air-gapped admin console. They requested a small POC (1 rack / 4x A100-equivalent or 2x L4 equivalent) and a dry-run checklist for security review. Conversation had many micro-decisions — captured below.
infra_inventory:
Customer-provided inventory (confirmed during workshop):
- 3 physical racks available in private colo (rack IDs: R12, R13, R14)
- Networking: spine/leaf fabric, VLAN segmentation available, out-of-band management via separate mgmt VLAN
- Compute targets: will provision 2 GPUs initially (they proposed 2xA10 or 4xT4 alternative) but can allocate 4 GPUs for the POC if needed
- Storage: NFS available in isolated VLAN; they prefer local NVMe for model cache and shared NFS for artifacts
- KMS: on-prem HSM (Thales) available, must integrate but cannot be internet-facing
- Identity: Okta for admin accounts; local AD for host auth
- Existing infra constraints: no internet egress allowed from model-serving VLAN without explicit exception
network_requirements:
Minimum flows discussed:
- Control-plane (Redwood admin console) should run in a separate management subnet with access via secure jump host (customer will host jump host).
- Model-serving nodes must not egress model weights outside the rack. Supportable patterns:
  1) Full offline bundle: model weights pre-loaded via encrypted disk images (preferred by security).
  2) Signed artifact server on isolated NFS (pull during maintenance window).
- TLS: mutual TLS required between services.
- Ports: propose 8443 (control plane), 2210 (internal RPC for KV cache sync), 50051 (gRPC for local SDK), optionally 6379 for redis shim if customer accepts it in mgmt VLAN.
- Monitoring: metrics exported on a dedicated port to Prometheus pull endpoint in mgmt VLAN only (no internet push).
- Network ops ask: can Redwood runtime function with no internet DNS? We noted name resolution can be local via /etc/hosts or internal DNS — action item created.
security_and_compliance:
Key constraints from MedicaSys security team:
- PHI cannot leave premises; logs containing PHI must be filtered before any export.
- HSM must hold signing key for model artifacts and disk images. Redwood must support HSM-backed signing or provide a signing API that runs in customer environment.
- Audit logs retention: min 2 years in immutable storage.
- Baseline hardening: CIS-like host hardening preferred; customer will run SCAP scanning during POC.
- Attestation: they asked for SBOM for all runtime binaries and a signed manifest for container images or RPMs.
- Regulatory check: need to confirm EU data residency equivalence for future rollouts (note: this POC is US-only).
deployment_options_evaluation:
Option A: Encrypted disk image bundle (offline). Pros: simplest for zero-egress, no runtime package checks once bootstrapped. Cons: heavier operational lift for updates; requires secure media transfer.
Option B: Airgapped package repository (RPMs/DEBs) served from isolated artifact server. Pros: easier incremental updates, integrates with patching. Cons: still needs pull window scheduling and signed artifact verification.
Option C: Containerized runtime with offline OCI registry (tarball transport + local registry). Pros: close to hosted experience, reproducible images. Cons: need registry bootstrap and may require more storage.
Recommendation: start POC with Option C (OCI tarball + local registry) and provide an offline signing tool that integrates with their HSM. If that surface proves too heavy, fall back to Option A for quickest validation.
risks_and_blockers:
- HSM integration unknowns: we need API/connector details (PKCS#11 endpoints, access policies).
- Model licensing: some open models have license terms that complicate offline redistribution; legal needs to vet.
- Monitoring/alerts: customer requires no cloud-based alerting; we need to deliver a runbook for on-prem alerting and fallback when operator is offline.
- Storage performance: NVMe sizing for KV cache not yet confirmed — may impact throughput.
- Lead time for physical media transfer: security wants a sealed transfer process for initial weights — logistics to be defined.
recommendations:
1) Build a small airgap POC package: OCI tarball + local registry bootstrap script + offline signing tool (HSM-backed).
2) Provide a step-by-step security dry-run checklist (SCAP, SBOM, attestations) for MedicaSys security team to pre-approve.
3) Prepare an offline metrics collector bundle and a local alerting playbook (Prometheus + Alertmanager local-only).
4) Schedule a follow-up session to walk HSM integration with their security engineer and get sample PKCS#11 config.
5) Run a smoke test on smaller instance (2 GPUs) to validate NVMe cache sizing before scaling to 4 GPUs.
